target_units.text: Make him drunk, for he magnified himself against the Lord. Moab will strike with his hand and become a laughingstock himself.

relationship: shared triad of trap, fear and pit
rationale: Jeremiah places trap, fear and pit upon resident Moab. Isaiah announces the same three dangers in the order fear, pit and trap upon the earth's inhabitants, giving a close verbal counterpart with a different order and broader audience.
source_text: Trap, fear, and pit are upon you, resident Moab.

target_units.text: Fear, pit and trap are upon you who dwell on the earth!

relationship: repeated inescapable progression from fear to pit to trap
rationale: Both passages say one fleeing fear falls into a pit and one climbing from the pit is caught by a trap. Jeremiah applies the sequence to Moab's year of visitation, while Isaiah continues with opened heavenly windows and shaken foundations.
source_text: One who flees from fear will fall into the pit, and one who climbs from the pit will be caught in the trap, for I will bring these things upon Moab in the year of her visitation.

target_units.text: Whoever flees the fear will fall into the pit, and whoever climbs from the pit will be caught by the trap, because windows from heaven have opened and the earth’s foundations will be shaken.

relationship: parallel cup of unmixed wine in the Lord's hand
rationale: Jeremiah is told to take the Lord's cup of unmixed wine for the nations. The psalm likewise describes a cup in the Lord's hand containing unmixed wine, then speaks of its mixture and the earth's sinners drinking, preserving the supplied wording's combination.
source_text: Thus said the Lord, Israel’s God: Take this cup of unmixed wine from My hand, and give it to all the nations to whom I send you to drink,

target_units.text: For in the Lord’s hand is a cup of unmixed wine, full of mixture; and He tilted from this into that, but its dregs were not emptied out; all the earth’s sinners will drink.

relationship: parallel wine causing disorder among nations
rationale: Jeremiah says the cup's recipients will drink, vomit and become mad before the sword. Jeremiah 28 depicts Babylon as a golden cup whose wine the nations drank and were shaken; the source of the wine and exact effects are worded differently.
source_text: and they will drink, vomit, and go mad before the sword I am sending among them.

target_units.text: Babylon was a golden cup in the Lord’s hand, making the whole earth drunk. Nations drank her wine; therefore they were shaken.

relationship: same-chapter execution of the command to distribute the cup
rationale: Jeremiah says he took the cup from the Lord and gave it to the nations to which he was sent. This explicitly carries out the earlier instruction to take that cup and make those nations drink it.
source_text: And I took the cup from the Lord’s hand and gave it to the nations to whom the Lord sent me to drink:

target_units.text: Thus said the Lord, Israel’s God: Take this cup of unmixed wine from My hand, and give it to all the nations to whom I send you to drink,

relationship: related desolation and hissing announced against Judah
rationale: The cup list names Jerusalem and Judah's cities, kings and rulers, destined for desolation and hissing. The earlier oracle to Judah likewise announces devastation and hissing from the northern force, followed by service among the nations.
source_text: Jerusalem, Judah’s cities, Judah’s kings, and its rulers, to make them a desolation, an untrodden place, and a hissing;

target_units.text: behold, I am sending and will take the clan from the north and bring them against this land, its inhabitants, and all the surrounding nations. I will lay them waste and make them a ruin, a hissing, and eternal reproach.
And I will remove from them the sound of joy and delight, the sound of bridegroom and bride, the fragrance of ointment and the light of a lamp.
And all the land will become a ruin, and they will serve among the nations for seventy years.

relationship: particular Egypt oracle for a named recipient of the cup
rationale: The cup list includes Pharaoh, his servants, nobles and people. Jeremiah 26 expressly introduces Babylon's king coming to strike Egypt and describes the defeat that the Lord brings, supplying a particular judgment oracle for this listed nation.
source_text: and Pharaoh king of Egypt, his servants, his nobles, and all his people;

target_units.text: What the Lord spoke through Jeremiah concerning Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon coming to cut down Egypt’s land:
Announce to Migdol and proclaim to Memphis. Say, Take your position and prepare, for the sword has devoured your smilax growth.
Why did Apis flee? Your choice calf did not remain, for the Lord disabled him.

relationship: parallel judgment naming the four Philistine cities
rationale: Jeremiah lists Ashkelon, Gaza, Ekron and Ashdod among recipients of judgment's cup. Zephaniah likewise names Gaza, Ashkelon, Ashdod and Ekron and assigns each its downfall, a particularly close city grouping.
source_text: and all his mixed population, all the Philistine kings, Ashkelon, Gaza, Ekron, and Ashdod’s remnant;

target_units.text: For Gaza will be plundered and Ashkelon will disappear; Ashdod will be cast out at midday and Ekron uprooted.

relationship: particular judgment upon Moab and Ammon within the cup's list
rationale: Jeremiah lists Idumea, Moab and Ammon among the cup's recipients. Zephaniah supplies an explicit judgment upon two of these, Moab and Ammon, because of their reproach and arrogance; it does not give the Idumea portion of this unit.
source_text: and Idumea, the Moabite land, and Ammon’s sons;

target_units.text: I heard Moab’s reproaches and the Ammonites’ blows, with which they reproached My people and exalted themselves against My borders.

Therefore, as I live, says the Lord of powers, the God of Israel, Moab will be like Sodom and the Ammonites like Gomorrah, and Damascus abandoned like a heap on a threshing floor and vanished forever. My people’s remnant will plunder them; My nation’s remnant will inherit them.
This will be theirs for their arrogance, because they reproached and exalted themselves against the Lord Almighty.

relationship: particular judgment upon Tyre and Sidon within the cup's list
rationale: Jeremiah names Tyre and Sidon's kings among recipients of the cup. Joel likewise directly addresses Tyre and Sidon and announces recompense for their actions against Judah and Jerusalem, giving a particular counterpart for the named coastal cities.
source_text: and all Tyre’s kings, Sidon’s kings, and the kings across the sea;

target_units.text: What have you to do with Me, Tyre and Sidon and all Galilee of foreigners? Are you repaying Me a recompense? Or do you bear a sharp grudge against Me? I will speedily repay your recompense upon your heads,
because you took My silver and gold and brought My chosen and beautiful things into your temples,
and sold the sons of Judah and the sons of Jerusalem to the sons of the Greeks, so as to thrust them out of their own borders.
Look, I am rousing them from the place to which you sold them, and I will repay your recompense upon your heads,
and I will sell your sons and daughters into the hands of the sons of Judah, and they will sell them into captivity to a nation far away, because the Lord has spoken.”

relationship: particular Teman and Dedan warnings within the cup's list
rationale: Jeremiah 32 lists Dedan and Teman among those receiving the cup. Jeremiah 30 explicitly describes Teman's lost wisdom and commands Dedan to go deep to dwell amid visitation, supplying particular warnings for those two names without explaining every other listed group.
source_text: and Dedan, Teman, Ros, and everyone shorn about his face;

target_units.text: For Idumea, thus says the Lord: There is no longer wisdom in Teman; counsel perished from the discerning; their wisdom went away.
Their place was deceived. Go deep to dwell, inhabitants of Dedan, for he did difficult things; I brought them upon him at the time I visited him.

relationship: related judgment lists including wilderness dwellers
rationale: The cup list includes mixed populations dwelling in the wilderness. Jeremiah 9's visitation list likewise ends with wilderness dwellers and also names several surrounding peoples found in Jeremiah 32; its face-clipping description is distinct from the mixed-populations wording.
source_text: and all the mixed populations lodging in the wilderness;

target_units.text: Behold, days are coming, says the Lord, and I will visit all who have been circumcised in their foreskins:

Egypt and Judea and Edom and the sons of Ammon and the sons of Moab and everyone who clips the hair around his face, those dwelling in the wilderness; because all the nations are uncircumcised in flesh, and all Israel’s house are uncircumcised in their hearts.

relationship: particular Elam oracle within the cup's list
rationale: Jeremiah 32 includes Elam's kings among those receiving the cup. Jeremiah 25 announces the breaking of Elam's bow, dispersion and the sending away of its king and nobles, giving a particular counterpart for Elam without extending those details to the separate Persian kings.
source_text: and all Elam’s kings and all the Persian kings;

target_units.text: Thus says the Lord: Let Elam’s bow be shattered, the beginning of their dominion.
I will bring upon Elam four winds from heaven’s four ends and scatter them among all these winds. There will be no nation where Elam’s outcasts do not come.
I will terrify them before their enemies who seek their lives and bring calamities upon them according to the anger of My wrath. I will send My sword after them until they are consumed.
I will set My throne in Elam and send king and nobles away from there.
In the last days I will turn back Elam’s captivity, says the Lord.

relationship: parallel judgment encompassing assembled nations and kings
rationale: Jeremiah expands the cup list to kings far and near and kingdoms across the earth. Zephaniah likewise describes judgment for assemblies of nations and kings under God's wrath, with all the earth affected.
source_text: and all the kings from the east, far and near, each with his brother, and all the kingdoms upon the face of the earth.

target_units.text: Therefore wait for Me, says the Lord, for the day of My rising for testimony. My judgment is for assemblies of nations, to receive kings and pour all My furious wrath upon them; for all the earth will be consumed in My jealous fire.

relationship: parallel command to drink the Lord's cup in judgment
rationale: Jeremiah commands drinking and drunkenness and predicts falling before the coming sword. Habakkuk likewise commands drinking and shaking because the cup of the Lord's right hand has come around, there contrasting dishonor with former glory.
source_text: And say to them: Thus said the Lord Almighty: Drink, get drunk, and vomit; you will fall and certainly not rise before the sword I am sending among you.

target_units.text: Drink, you too, a fullness of dishonor instead of glory; be tossed and shaken! The cup of the Lord’s right hand has come around to you, and dishonor has gathered upon your glory.

relationship: parallel refusal of exemption from drinking judgment
rationale: Jeremiah 32 says those refusing the cup certainly must drink. Jeremiah 30 similarly says the addressed one will not be cleared and certainly will drink, preserving the explicit denial of escape from the cup.
source_text: And when they are unwilling to receive the cup from your hand to drink, say: Thus said the Lord: You will certainly drink.

target_units.text: For thus said the Lord: Those for whom there was no law to drink the cup drank it. And you, though acquitted, certainly will not be acquitted, for you will certainly drink.

relationship: analogous argument from judgment beginning with God's own people
rationale: Jeremiah argues that judgment beginning with the city bearing God's name does not leave the other nations unpunished. Peter likewise asks what awaits disobedient people if judgment begins with God's house; the city and the Christian community are distinct settings.
source_text: Because I am beginning to bring harm in the city upon which My name was named, and you will certainly not be cleansed, because I am summoning a sword against those dwelling upon the earth.

target_units.text: For it is time for judgment to begin from the house of God; and if it begins first from us, what will be the outcome for those who disobey the good news of God?

relationship: parallel divine voice from a sacred location within judgment of nations
rationale: Jeremiah announces the Lord giving His voice from His holy place on high. Joel likewise describes the Lord crying from Zion and giving His voice from Jerusalem as heaven and earth shake; the stated locations and consequences remain distinct.
source_text: And prophesy these words against them and say: The Lord will give an oracle from on high; from His holy place He will raise His voice. He will give an oracular word over His place, and they will answer with Aidad, like grape-gatherers. And upon those dwelling upon the earth,

target_units.text: The Lord will cry out from Zion and give His voice from Jerusalem; heaven and earth will shake. But the Lord will spare His people, and the Lord will strengthen the sons of Israel.

relationship: parallel judgment of all flesh by the Lord's sword
rationale: Jeremiah announces the Lord's judgment against all flesh and ungodly people given to the sword. Isaiah likewise says all flesh is judged by His sword and many are wounded by the Lord, giving a close combination of agent, scope and weapon.
source_text: destruction comes upon a part of the earth, because the Lord has a judgment among the nations. He enters judgment with all flesh, and the ungodly were given to the sword, says the Lord.

target_units.text: For by the Lord’s fire all the earth will be judged, and by His sword all flesh; many will be wounded by the Lord.

relationship: parallel storm imagery accompanying divine wrath
rationale: Jeremiah announces calamities passing between nations and a great whirlwind from the earth's extremity. Isaiah compares the Lord's chariots with a storm when He renders vengeance in wrath; the shared storm image does not make the whirlwind and chariots identical.
source_text: Thus said the Lord: Behold, evils come from nation to nation, and a great whirlwind goes out from the earth’s farthest end.

target_units.text: For behold, the Lord will come like fire, and His chariots like a storm, to render vengeance in wrath and rejection in a flame of fire.

relationship: parallel unburied dead upon the earth under judgment
rationale: Jeremiah 32 describes those wounded by the Lord lying unburied across the earth. Jeremiah 16 likewise announces deaths without burial, also denying mourning and describing bodies upon the earth's surface exposed to animals; it does not use the source's dung description.
source_text: And those wounded by the Lord on the Lord’s day will lie from one part of the earth to another. They will certainly not be buried; they will be dung upon the earth’s face.

target_units.text: They will die a diseased death; they will not be mourned or buried. They will be an example upon the earth’s surface, and for the earth’s wild beasts and heaven’s birds; they will fall by the sword and be consumed by famine.

relationship: parallel slaughter pictured through selected sheep or rams
rationale: Jeremiah addresses shepherds and rams, announces the fulfillment of their slaughter days and predicts their falling like choice rams. Jeremiah 28 likewise describes bringing the condemned down like lambs to slaughter and like rams with young goats, applying the flock image to another judgment scene.
source_text: Raise a shout, shepherds, and cry out; beat yourselves in mourning, rams of the sheep, because your days for slaughter have been fulfilled, and you will fall like choice rams.

target_units.text: I will bring them down like lambs to slaughter and like rams with young goats.

relationship: parallel denial of flight and survival
rationale: Jeremiah denies flight to shepherds and salvation to the rams of the sheep. Amos likewise says flight will perish and the swift, armed and mounted will not escape, giving a parallel collapse of presumed means of survival with different addressed figures.
source_text: And flight will perish from the shepherds, and salvation from the rams of the sheep.

relationship: parallel sound of shepherds lamenting a devastating loss
rationale: Jeremiah announces a sound of shepherds crying because the Lord destroyed their grazing places. Zechariah likewise announces shepherds lamenting because their greatness suffered; the target names their lost greatness rather than repeating the grazing-place clause.
source_text: A sound of shepherds crying and of sheep and rams shouting, because the Lord destroyed their grazing places,

target_units.text: A sound of shepherds lamenting, for their greatness has suffered! A sound of lions roaring, for the Jordan’s proud swelling has suffered!

relationship: parallel removal of peace under the Lord's judgment
rationale: Jeremiah says the remnants of peace cease before the Lord's fierce wrath. Jeremiah 12 likewise denies peace to any flesh when the Lord's sword devours from one end of the earth to the other, placing lost peace within sweeping judgment.
source_text: and the remnants of peace will cease before the anger of My fury.

target_units.text: Upon every passage through the wilderness those bringing misery came, because the Lord’s sword will devour from one end of the earth to the other; there is no peace for any flesh.

relationship: parallel divine lion imagery and departure
rationale: Jeremiah describes the Lord leaving His lodging like a lion as the land becomes untrodden. Hosea likewise likens Him to a lion that seizes and goes away, then speaks of returning to His place; the differing directions do not identify Jeremiah's lodging with a particular building.
source_text: Like a lion He abandoned His lodging, because their land became an untrodden place before the great sword.
